title: Private upgrade: gate gateway rollout on control plane readiness + tune timeouts
author: Ines Carvalho
description: Context: During the end-to-end Private upgrade rehearsal we hit an edge case where the gateway Deployment rolled and started serving before the control plane was ready to accept traffic. In practice this showed up as intermittent 502s from the gateway while the control plane pod was still in CrashLoopBackOff / warming caches, and in one case the gateway never recovered because its boot-time discovery call exceeded the default timeout and the pod entered a backoff loop. Root cause: our chart ordering and readiness semantics allow the gateway rollout to proceed as soon as its own pods are schedulable, but do not gate on control plane readiness during upgrades (especially when both components are being updated in the same Helm release). Changes in this PR: (1) Add a dedicated Helm hook Job `control-plane-ready-gate` that blocks the upgrade until the control plane readiness endpoint returns OK (configurable timeout + retries). (2) Wire `gateway` to start with conservative defaults and avoid failing hard during control plane warmup by tuning startup/readiness timeouts and making the initial connection retry window configurable via values. (3) Ensure the gate runs for both `pre-upgrade` and `post-upgrade` paths so we don’t roll the gateway while the control plane is mid-migration, and we validate readiness after the control plane update completes. Notes: This is specifically targeted at the Private upgrade/rollback workflow; hosted/dedicated aren’t impacted. The hook Job is namespaced and uses the same serviceAccount as other upgrade hooks; permissions are limited to GET on the control plane Service endpoint (no list/watch cluster-wide). Related: ENG-2320 (upgrade sequencing) and rehearsal follow-ups from the releases thread; this complements the installer-level ordering but keeps the chart safe when users run `helm upgrade` directly.
implementation_notes: The readiness gate Job uses `curl` against the in-cluster control plane service (`http://redwood-control-plane.<ns>.svc:8080/readyz`) with exponential-ish backoff (sleep increments) and an overall timeout. Default timeout is set to 8 minutes based on observed migration + warmup times in staging, with an upper bound recommendation of 15 minutes for slower on-prem disks. Gateway tuning: (a) set `startupProbe` to allow longer initial boot without flapping readiness, (b) increase `readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds` and `failureThreshold` so transient control plane unavailability during upgrade doesn’t eject pods too aggressively, and (c) introduce `gateway.controlPlane.connectRetryWindowSeconds` for the gateway container env var used by its bootstrap code. The hook Job is annotated with `helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade,post-upgrade` and `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` to avoid leaving Jobs around while still preserving failures for debugging when the Job fails. When the gate fails, Helm will fail the release, which is the desired behavior (installer can then initiate rollback).
testing: Staging rehearsal: simulated control plane slow start by adding artificial 3–4 minute warmup; verified Helm upgrade blocks at readiness gate and gateway does not roll until control plane returns ready
Forced control plane to fail readiness permanently; verified Helm upgrade fails with clear Job logs and does not proceed to gateway rollout
Smoke: `helm template` and `helm lint` on umbrella chart; verified hooks render correctly under `redwoodControlPlane.readinessGate.enabled=false`
Rollback rehearsal: after failed gate, re-ran upgrade after fixing control plane; verified subsequent `helm upgrade` succeeds and Jobs clean up
commits: Add control-plane readiness gate Job as pre/post-upgrade hook
Tune gateway probes and control plane connection retry window for upgrades
Document new values + upgrade sequencing note in chart README
Bump chart version and add changelog note
review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can we confirm the endpoint is stable across versions? Prefer /readyz over /healthz, and it should not require auth from inside the cluster. Also please ensure we don’t gate on the new version’s Service name if users override fullname templates.

Ines Carvalho (author): Good call. Switched to /readyz (existing) and used the chart’s computed fullname for service DNS via helper template. Added a note in README about overriding `fullnameOverride` and how the gate follows it.

Connor O'Brien: Hook-delete-policy should keep failed Jobs for debugging (at least until next run). Can we keep failures around? Also, are we comfortable with Helm upgrade failing hard here (installer expects a deterministic failure point)?

Ines Carvalho (author): Updated hook-delete-policy to only delete on success + before-hook-creation; failures remain so SRE/Support can grab logs. Yes, failing the release is desired; installer can surface the Job logs and initiate rollback.

Sean Gallagher: Default timeout 8m seems OK for staging but on-prem can be slower. Can we make the default slightly higher or at least document guidance? Also probe tuning: ensure we don’t mask real failures by making thresholds too forgiving.

Ines Carvalho (author): Kept 8m default but added docs recommending 12–15m for slower disks and included an explicit alerting note (SRE) that a prolonged readiness gate should page. Probe thresholds tuned to avoid flapping but still fail within ~30s of persistent unready after startup window.
Rafael Mendes: Please add a short snippet in the runbook docs on what to look at when the gate fails (Job logs, control plane pod logs, migration job status).
Ines Carvalho (author): Added a README section with troubleshooting steps and pointers; runbook update is tracked in ENG-2323 but I added enough here for immediate usage.
Connor O'Brien: LGTM after latest changes. Approving.
release_notes: Private Helm charts: upgrades now include a control-plane readiness gate to prevent gateway rollout before the control plane is ready. Adds configurable timeouts and probe tuning to reduce transient 502s during control plane warmup.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien
follow_ups: ENG-2323: Ensure runbook references the readiness gate failure mode and includes exact `kubectl logs job/<gate>` commands
ENG-2321: Emit a metric/log signal from installer when Helm upgrade fails due to readiness gate (for upgrade telemetry dashboards)
